subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi, around seventy, was found dead in white robes soaked dark around the torso, his rib cage caved in and a hollow in his chest where something had been removed. He was a scholar engaged in research on unfamiliar magical workings, annotated in multiple ink layers — Celestial, midnight blue, and purple — suggesting a progression of thought. His final notes, written in the freshest ink, were missing. He was likely murdered hours before discovery.
source_quote: Janussi — around seventy, white robes, vacant eyes aimed at nothing. The robes were soaked dark around the torso. His rib cage had been caved in. There was a hollow in his chest where something used to be.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi, the Keeper, was found dead with his rib cage caved in and heart removed; he was engaged in scholarly research on celestial workings and had recently annotated notes in midnight blue ink before his death.
source_quote: The quill on the floor had a nib covered in midnight blue ink — the last thing he touched.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan was the previous guard at the tower door, relieved before the party’s arrival; Tadric noted he looked more determined leaving than entering, suggesting he had encountered something significant before being removed from duty.
source_quote: Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan was the previous guard who was relieved before the investigators arrived.
source_quote: Bookwyrm told him Kalan had been relieved and that the four of us would be taking over.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch expects to be listened to and usually is.
source_quote: He'd been the one who wanted to put Daz in irons when we arrived... the posture of someone who expects to be listened to and usually is.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch has a gray-white beard, piercing blue eyes, and expects to be listened to.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch walked in. I recognized him — the gray-white beard, the piercing blue eyes, the posture of someone who expects to be listened to and usually is.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the gate warden of Candlekeep, a figure of authority with piercing eyes and an expectation of deference. He was recently asked by Janussi to tender his resignation due to concerns over mental decline and negligence. He was barred from entering or leaving the premises by Bookwyrm, who anticipated his arrival. His bow was correct but his eyes were not — indicating suppressed hostility. Grygum identified him as the first person to question.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the gate warden who was ordered to resign by Janussi the morning of the murder, cited for declining mental faculties and negligence. He has a piercing gaze and an authoritative posture, and his bow to Bookwyrm was correct — but his eyes were not. He is the first person the narrator plans to question.
source_quote: (Silent bow; eyes were not.)

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch previously wanted to put Daz in irons upon arrival at Candlekeep.
source_quote: He'd been the one who wanted to put Daz in irons when we arrived.

subject: Kazryn

source_quote: Then the weeping woman — Kazryn, apparently — showed up shortly after, wanting to see the body.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani arrived shortly after 8 a.m., distraught, and was permitted only a doorway view of the body; no further interaction occurred.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani, distraught, shortly after eight — allowed to see the body but only from the doorway.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani arrived shortly after eight, distraught, and was allowed to see the body only from the doorway.
source_quote: Then: Kazryn Nyantani, distraught, shortly after eight — allowed to see the body but only from the doorway.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn arrived distraught shortly after eight, permitted only to view the body from the doorway; her emotional state was noted but no action taken beyond containment.
source_quote: She was weeping, wanting to see the body.

source_quote: The Keeper of Tomes is dead!

subject: Miss Hollypocket
fact: Miss Hollypocket discovered Janussi's body and would never allow candles to burn down to nothing.

subject: Miss Hollypocket
fact: Miss Hollypocket was the servant who found Janussi’s body alongside A'lai Aivenmore. She is described as rigidly protocol-bound — she would never have allowed candles to burn down to nothing, implying Janussi had been dead before the candles extinguished.
source_quote: Miss Hollypocket would never have allowed the Keeper to let candles burn down to nothing. Full stop. It wasn't her way.

subject: Miss Hollypocket
fact: Miss Hollypocket, the housekeeper, discovered the body and is noted for her strict adherence to protocol — she would never allow candles to burn down to nothing, implying Janussi was dead before the candles extinguished.
source_quote: She would never have allowed the Keeper to let candles burn down to nothing.

subject: Oghma

subject: Pizwog

source_quote: He distributes what appears to be a religious tract, which turns out to be one of his own research papers — a syncretic analysis of different religions across the Sword Coast, deeply theoretical, internally inconsistent in ways I can tell are meaningful...

subject: Pizwog
fact: Pizwog is an ancient tortle scholar who distributes his own syncretic research papers on Sword Coast religions, and whose slow, deliberate manner and intellectual eccentricity are noted by observers.
source_quote: Pizwog, who is an ancient tortle and moves at the speed of an ancient tortle. I wait. He distributes what appears to be a religious tract, which turns out to be one of his own research papers.

subject: Pizwog
fact: Pizwog is an ancient tortle who moves at the speed of an ancient tortle.
source_quote: We are briefly interrupted by Pizwog, who is an ancient tortle and moves at the speed of an ancient tortle.

subject: Pizwog
fact: Pizwog is deeply theoretical and internally inconsistent in ways that are meaningful but not yet specified.
source_quote: a syncretic analysis of different religions across the Sword Coast, deeply theoretical, internally inconsistent in ways I can tell are meaningful without yet being able to specify how

subject: Sister Yvenne

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud is referenced as a great philosopher whose decisive moves and unrepeatable instants are mythologized, and whose name is invoked in theological schools of thought.
source_quote: Aye! It could have been Stroud, our great philosopher. It could have been, say, another party of adventurers.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud made the decisive move against a dragon who had spent four hundred years studying that exact position.
source_quote: I think about Stroud making the decisive move — the perfect throw, the unrepeatable instant — against a dragon who had spent four hundred years studying that exact position.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is absent from the Council meeting and her absence is questioned by Daral.
source_quote: why isn't Sylvira Savikas here?

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric confirmed attempts had been made to speak to the dead, but the dead were not speaking.
source_quote: The dead were not speaking.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric is a young human guard assigned to crowd control at the Keeper's Chambers; he admits his failure to observe internal actions, realizing too late that his role was insufficient for the gravity of the situation.
source_quote: His job was watching who came in and out, not what they did once inside.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric is a young human guard with a bowl-cut, assigned to crowd control at the tower entrance; he admitted his role was not observational and felt embarrassment upon realizing his job was insufficient for the scale of the event; he confirmed the timeline of arrivals and departures around the death of Janussi.
source_quote: I was told to make sure only the right people came in and out.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric understood his job had been crowd control, not observation, and realized he had failed to notice what people did inside the room.
source_quote: His job had been crowd control, not surveillance — watching who came in and out, not watching what they did once they were inside.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric was guarding the door and responsible for crowd control, not observation.
source_quote: Tadric was guarding the door: short, human, young, bowl-cut hair, the look of someone who takes his post seriously and is currently experiencing the professional anxiety of having his post become considerably more significant than expected.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric was standing guard at the door when the party arrived, young and human, trying to appear composed despite being rattled. He provided timeline details and confirmed protocol adherence. He admitted his role was crowd control, not surveillance, and showed regret over the oversight. He is a decent person who recognized the gap in procedure but felt powerless to fix it.
source_quote: Tadric admitted his job had been crowd control, not surveillance — watching who came in and out, not watching what they did once they were inside.

subject: The Bookwyrm
fact: The Bookwyrm arrived at nine, fresh from the baths, took a brief look at the scene, and confirmed the gate warden’s orders. Their presence was observational and authoritative, lending weight to procedural compliance.
source_quote: Then the Bookwyrm at nine, in from the baths, taking a brief look before confirming the gate warden's orders.

subject: The Bronze Dragonborn
fact: The bronze dragonborn in bejeweled robes is demanding dismissal of the gate warden, asserting blame and positioning himself as prosecutor with full awareness of his authority and appearance.
source_quote: The gate warden needs to be dismissed with immediate effect! This happened on HIS watch!

subject: The Dowdy Halfling
fact: The dowdy halfling with pince-nez is pushing for determination of a successor before addressing murder, prioritizing bureaucratic procedure over crisis response.
source_quote: First, we must determine if Janussi named a successor—

subject: The First Reader
fact: The First Reader is a senior authority at Candlekeep who bypasses standard protocols to summon the party directly after the Keeper of Tomes’ death, indicating deep trust in their abilities and a desire to control the narrative before institutional forces intervene.
source_quote: The first reader sent me! ... She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Gate Warden
fact: The Gate Warden arrived at eight with Tadric and returned at eleven for a full investigation. He was described as careful not to disturb evidence. His demeanor shifted to determination after inspecting the scene, suggesting he identified something significant — possibly a clue — that he had not yet decided how to act upon.
source_quote: He definitely looked more determined after he walked out. Determined means he found something and hadn't decided what to do with it yet.

subject: The Keeper
fact: The Keeper falls — dead, with no one speaking, the fire warm, and that was enough for tonight.
source_quote: *The keeper falls.* I didn't say anything. The fire was warm. That was enough for tonight.

subject: The Keeper of Tomes
fact: The Keeper of Tomes is a high-ranking institutional figure at Candlekeep who has been found dead under mysterious circumstances, prompting the First Reader to summon the party through the emerald door before the Avowed awaken, suggesting a deliberate cover-up or controlled investigation.
source_quote: The Keeper of Tomes is dead! She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Messenger
fact: The messenger is a commoner-born youth entrusted with urgent news of the Keeper’s death; his breathless urgency and visible delight in being chosen suggest he is an unwitting pawn in a larger scheme of information control.
source_quote: Quick! The first reader sent me! The Keeper of Tomes is dead! She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Messenger
fact: The messenger is commoner-born, boyish, delighted by his urgency, and sprinted across old stone corridors to deliver the news that the Keeper of Tomes is dead.
source_quote: He was commoner-born, I could see that much — enthusiastic in the way of someone who has been trusted with important information for the first time and found the experience clarifying. Boyish. Very slightly delighted by his own urgency

subject: The Narrator
fact: The Narrator is the investigator who observes, records, and interprets the room like a Bahamut text — reading not what is said, but what is conspicuously not said. They file distinctions, note pauses, and plan questions before speaking. They are the only one who recognizes that the real value on the table is not the books, but the excuse to poke everywhere.
source_quote: See, this gives us an excuse to poke our nose in everywhere. That's valuable.

subject: The Narrator
fact: The narrator is an observer and thinker who has not previously been aware of their own theological position, but has arrived at an intuitive belief in a universe governed by fixed points and silent conspiratorial constraint.
source_quote: I am sitting with this — genuinely sitting with it... when I notice that none of them quite fit what I actually think. Which is inconvenient, because I had not previously been aware that I actually thought anything about this.

subject: The Party (Orc, Dragonborn, Dwarf, Drow)
fact: The party consists of four non-human outsiders, whose presence is noted and categorized by the Council as 'unknown provenance,' and whose arrival has shifted the focus of the crisis from murder to epistemological novelty.
source_quote: They cataloged us immediately — orc, dragonborn, dwarf, drow — and sorted us into the correct drawer: arrivals. unknown provenance. examine.

subject: The Purple-Robed Watcher
fact: The purple-robed watcher at the Chapter House entrance assessed the party briefly and stepped aside without challenge, having been pre-instructed to expect them.
source_quote: A purple-robed watcher stood at the entrance, assessed us briefly, and stepped aside. No challenge. They had been told to expect us.

subject: The Slender Human
fact: The slender human with heavy wrinkles is prioritizing the identification of the murderer, demonstrating the only clear tactical clarity in the council’s chaos.
source_quote: First, we must find the murderer!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked about the timeline and noted the Gate Warden’s demeanor after his inspection.
source_quote: I asked. 'Did it look like he discovered something?' About the gate warden. 'He definitely looked more determined after he walked out.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dragonborn investigator who consistently focuses on structural truths: he identifies testimony as evidence, proposes examining people as objects of inquiry, and notes the fragility of the corpse due to elapsed time since death.
source_quote: But your testimony is evidence. Maybe you are evidence, and we should examine you.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic negotiator and social strategist who framed the party’s involvement in terms of pop culture (Poirot, Colombo) and philosophical claims. He insisted on remuneration — one book each — and pushed for carte blanche access to the library. He challenged Bookwyrm’s alibi with direct questioning, demonstrating investigative instincts. He clarified his own non-participation in Dawnbringer’s discovery, showing self-awareness.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the investigator who pressed for full library access, demanded remuneration in the form of books, and insisted on examining all parties — including Bookwyrm — after she withheld evidence. He framed the investigation as a matter of divine mandate and scholarly rigor, referencing Poirot and Colombo as intellectual ancestors.
source_quote: Are we supposed to investigate if we can't poke around?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mentions he and his wife have been watching a great deal of Poirot lately.
source_quote: Thorin noted that he and his wife had been watching a great deal of Poirot lately.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth believes ancient agency rules and the dragons follow their elders out of trust.
source_quote: The Draconic school says ancient agency rules. Protanther honored Stroud's move because Protanther is honorable... The metallic dragons followed Protanther because they trust their elders.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth believes divine providence prevails and mortals serve as instruments of Bahamut.
source_quote: The Bahamutian school says divine providence prevails. Bahamut moved his pieces beforehand. The mortals served as instruments.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth believes mortal choice is sovereign, the gods exist, the dragons exist, and Providence may or may not exist.
source_quote: The Stroudite school says mortal choice is sovereign. The gods exist. The dragons exist. Providence may or may not exist.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth has been keeping this corner of the library for forty-one years and knows what a fashion looks like.
source_quote: He has been keeping this corner of the library for forty-one years, he says, and he knows what a fashion looks like.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth holds the strong-weak hypothesis: a strong Stroudite denies fixed points, a strong Bahamutian affirms them, and a weak Bahamutian operates outside them.
source_quote: He calls it a compromise of the Bahamutian school. He calls me a weak Stroudite — a strong Stroudite holds there are no fixed points at all — and a strong Bahamutian around fixed points, and a weak Bahamutian outside of them. He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a scholar who formalizes the 'strong-weak hypothesis,' assigns theological schools to Stroud and Bahamut, and collects Stroudite papers with ritualistic intensity.
source_quote: Vareth calls it a compromise of the Bahamutian school. He calls me a weak Stroudite — a strong Stroudite holds there are no fixed points at all — and a strong Bahamutian around fixed points, and a weak Bahamutian outside of them.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a senior librarian at Candlekeep who has maintained his side office for forty-one years, exhibits deep institutional restraint, and is actively developing a new theological framework regarding mortal agency and fixed points of cosmic constraint.
source_quote: Vareth, behind me, has the expression of a man exercising tremendous institutional restraint across approximately five minutes of tortle handoff. He remains respectful throughout.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is an aging scholar with forty-one years in a side office at Candlekeep, deeply immersed in theological and philosophical debates, and has just been inspired by an offhand remark to formulate a new school of thought — the Grygum school — which posits fixed points of cosmic constraint amid otherwise free agency.
source_quote: He calls it a compromise of the Bahamutian school... He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: Vof Klownits

subject: witness count

source_quote: Janussi found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket... Gate Warden arrived with Tadric... Kazryn Nyantani... Fheminor Scrivenbark... Bookwyrm at nine

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir concluded the rib cage was smashed by multiple close, deliberate axe blows, the heart was missing, and the blood was localized — a pattern inconsistent with a violent death, suggesting the victim was already dead before the chest was opened.
source_quote: The question: was he dead before his heart was hacked out?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow who quietly questioned whether the cat might be something more than it appears; his single word — 'Is it?' — caused Fembris to reconsider his position.
source_quote: Is it?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed that the rib cage had been smashed by multiple blows with something like an axe and noted the blood pattern suggested death preceded the chest opening.
source_quote: Zalthir looked more carefully than I did. He's better at the precise reading of things — the monk's eye for controlled force. His verdict: the rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate. The heart was missing. No other organs. And the blood was localized.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir performed a precise forensic analysis of the wound, determining the rib cage was shattered by multiple deliberate blows with an axe-like weapon, and that the heart was removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection.
source_quote: The heart was missing. No other organs. And the blood was localized — wrong pattern for a violent death.

subject: annotated book title
fact: The book being annotated with blue ink was The Golden Ass.
source_quote: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room.

subject: Asha Vandree's Chain Mail

source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: Asha Vandree's chain mail theological document

source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence, written in a hand that wanted very much to seem incidental.

subject: bag of holding

subject: Celestial notes

subject: Dawnbringer

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sword housed in her scabbard that claims to have been found after two thousand years.
source_quote: Dawnbringer, housed in her scabbard, took the opportunity to note that we must surely be the greatest discoverers of all, having found her tomb after two thousand years.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is set against the wall within reach in the hearth room.
source_quote: set Dawnbringer against the wall within reach

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer, the party’s weapon, is now kept within reach but not drawn in the House of Rest — a ritualized negotiation of safety and restraint that mirrors the broader tension between freedom and constraint in the Grygum school.
source_quote: I set Dawnbringer against the wall within reach — close but not drawn, which had become its own negotiation over the weeks.

subject: Dawnbringer's age
fact: Dawnbringer was found in a tomb after two thousand years.
source_quote: having found her tomb after two thousand years

subject: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber

source_quote: Fembris warned us about the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber inside. One of the Avowed had died in it, he said, which was why the Keeper's permission was now required.

source_quote: Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it.

subject: Glabbagool's Bag of Holding

source_quote: The grey ooze had been confined to the bag of holding for most of the day... he was done with it. He wanted out.

subject: Ilvara's Prayer Book

source_quote: I think about Ilvara's prayer book. The Zuggtmoy marginalia.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book contains Zuggtmoy marginalia, suggesting hidden theological alignments and deliberate obfuscation within sacred texts.

subject: linen ink carrier
fact: A wicker basket held a linen ink carrier, slightly damp — the vessel that had contained the spilled midnight blue ink. It had not been cleaned or moved, preserving evidence of the spill’s timing.
source_quote: A wicker basket nearby holding a linen ink carrier, slightly damp, which had been the vessel for the ink now pooling from the spilled pot.

subject: marble statue and pedestal

source_quote: The marble statue and its pedestal were on the floor.

subject: midnight blue ink notes

source_quote: To the other side, a larger pile of notes pinned under a quartz weight, with more annotations on top in midnight blue ink — and below those, older notes in purple.

subject: Midnight Blue Ink Pot and Quill
fact: An ink pot spilled on the desk, with a quill on the floor bearing fresh midnight blue ink — the last physical trace of Janussi’s activity before death, indicating he was writing moments before being killed.
source_quote: The quill had gone with it. Neither the ink nor the quill had been moved since.

subject: missing heart
fact: The heart was removed as a precautionary measure to block resurrection magic, and its absence is a deliberate signal or safeguard, not random violence.
source_quote: It was a message. Or a precaution.

subject: Notes
fact: The notes are picked up as the party prepares to move, indicating they are essential tools for recording and navigating the unfolding events.
source_quote: I picked up my notes.

subject: notes
fact: Zalthir picked up his notes before following the messenger.
source_quote: I picked up my notes.

subject: oil paintings
fact: Oil paintings of stern-faced sages in various states of disapproval line every staircase in the Candlekeep bastion.
source_quote: Oil paintings on every staircase, stern-faced sages in various states of disapproval

subject: One Book Each (Copied at the House of the Binder)
fact: The proposed remuneration for the investigators is one book each, copied at the House of the Binder, to be delivered only upon successful completion of the investigation. This is a symbolic, conditional payment — not for labor, but for discretion.
source_quote: One book each, copied at the House of the Binder, upon successful completion.

subject: Pizwog's research paper
fact: The narrator tucks Pizwog's research paper into his satchel.
source_quote: I tuck it into my satchel.

subject: prophecy inventory
fact: Candlekeep maintains an inventory of unfulfilled prophecies from Alaundo.
source_quote: What remained was the unfulfilled inventory

subject: purple ink
fact: Purple ink was used for older notes on Janussi’s desk, predating the recent midnight blue annotations.
source_quote: a larger pile of notes pinned under a quartz weight, with more annotations on top in midnight blue ink — and below those, older notes in purple.

subject: quartz weight
fact: A quartz weight was used to pin down a pile of notes in the Keeper's Chambers.
source_quote: a larger pile of notes pinned under a quartz weight, with more annotations on top in midnight blue ink

subject: quill
fact: A quill with a nib covered in midnight blue ink was found on the floor near the desk.
source_quote: A quill on the floor. Nib covered in midnight blue.

subject: quill ink residue
fact: The quill on the floor had a nib covered in midnight blue ink.
source_quote: A quill on the floor. Nib covered in midnight blue.

subject: quill with midnight blue nib
fact: A quill lay on the floor with its nib coated in midnight blue ink, matching the spilled ink pot. It had not been moved since the spill, indicating it fell during the attack or shortly after.
source_quote: A quill on the floor. Nib covered in midnight blue.

subject: safe contents
fact: Blue gems and empty pouches were scattered on the floor in front of the opened safe.
source_quote: The safe on the far wall had been opened. Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it.

subject: Sava game set
fact: A Sava game set is on the table in the guard chamber.
source_quote: It contains a zurkhwood table and three chairs, a smaller side table, and a Sava game set on the table

subject: seven-armed bronze candelabra
fact: A seven-armed bronze candelabra had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles in the Keeper's Chambers.
source_quote: The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

subject: spellbook title
fact: The spellbook open on the desk was titled The Discoveries.
source_quote: A spellbook sat open in the center of the desk: The Discoveries.

subject: Stroudite papers
fact: A stack of Stroudite papers, marked and annotated, represents a codified body of theological thought that was accidentally created and is now being curated by Vareth.
source_quote: Then he hands me a stack of Stroudite papers, barely able to contain himself, and rushes off to begin his own research.

subject: tapestries
fact: Heavy tapestries hang in the Candlekeep bastion and could conceal anything or nothing.
source_quote: The tapestries were heavy and could conceal anything or nothing.

subject: Tapestries of the Bastion
fact: The heavy tapestries lining the bastion’s corridors are capable of concealing threats or secrets, contributing to an atmosphere of latent danger.
source_quote: The tapestries were heavy and could conceal anything or nothing.

subject: The Confidentiality Papers
fact: The Confidentiality Papers are legal documents required before any investigation proceeds. They bind participants to secrecy, and their existence signals that the Council fears exposure more than they fear the murder.
source_quote: Confidentiality papers first.

subject: The Death Rite
fact: A death rite has already been performed on Janussi’s corpse by the Gate Warden prior to the party’s arrival; this renders the rite unusable for another attempt for a significant duration, delaying any spiritual inquiry.
source_quote: Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.

subject: The Discoveries
fact: The spellbook titled The Discoveries was open on the desk in the Keeper's Chambers.
source_quote: A spellbook sat open in the center of the desk: The Discoveries.

subject: The Discoveries (spellbook)
fact: A spellbook titled The Discoveries lay open on the desk, annotated in Celestial script with academic musings on unfamiliar magical workings — likely Janussi’s own research. It was undisturbed and central to the scene.
source_quote: A spellbook sat open in the center of the desk: The Discoveries. To one side, notes in Celestial, generic academic work, someone musing on unfamiliar workings and how they might be performed.

subject: The Discoveries (Spellbook)
fact: An open spellbook on the desk containing Janussi’s research on celestial workings, annotated with recent midnight blue ink and older purple notes; it was the focus of his final scholarly efforts.
source_quote: Notes in Celestial... annotations in midnight blue ink — and below those, older notes in purple.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The Golden Ass was the book Janussi was annotating in midnight blue ink, but it was missing from the room.
source_quote: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room.

subject: The Golden Ass (Missing Book)
fact: The book Janussi was actively annotating in midnight blue ink — 'The Golden Ass' — is missing from the room, suggesting it was taken deliberately to conceal his final research or its implications.
source_quote: Whatever Janussi had been working on most recently... was gone. That felt deliberate.

subject: The Golden Ass (missing book)
fact: The book The Golden Ass, which was being annotated in the freshest ink, was missing from the room. Its removal indicates the killer sought to conceal Janussi’s final research — the likely motive for the murder.
source_quote: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room.

subject: theological document
fact: The theological document with Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence is in Asha Vandree's chain mail.
source_quote: The theological document from Asha Vandree's chain mail — the Lolth/Zuggtmoy equivalence

subject: The Safe
fact: The safe on the far wall was opened, with blue gems and empty pouches scattered — the thief ignored the gems, indicating the target was something more valuable than jewelry.
source_quote: The thief had looked at the gems, decided they weren't what he came for, and left them.

subject: Tobacco Smoke
fact: Lingering tobacco smoke in the sealed chamber, despite no recent smoking — indicating the room had been closed since before the murder, and the killer or victim had smoked prior to death.
source_quote: The smoke was old. Nobody smokes in a sealed room and leaves smoke that lingers for hours unless the room has been sealed for hours.

subject: wicker basket
fact: A wicker basket containing a damp linen ink carrier was found near the desk.
source_quote: A wicker basket nearby holding a linen ink carrier, slightly damp, which had been the vessel for the ink now pooling from the spilled pot.

subject: Zuggtmoy marginalia
fact: The Zuggtmoy marginalia are in Ilvara's prayer book.
source_quote: The Zuggtmoy marginalia.

subject: absence of Sylvira Savikas
fact: The absence of Sylvira Savikas from the Council of Twelve is a pointed mystery, implying her potential involvement in the murder, suppression of information, or intentional withdrawal.
source_quote: why isn't Sylvira Savikas here?

subject: Bahamut text
fact: Grygum reads the room the way he reads a Bahamut text — for what is conspicuously not said.
source_quote: I read the room the way I read a Bahamut text — not for what it says, but for what it is conspicuously not saying.

subject: Bookwyrm’s alibi
fact: When asked where she was during the murder, Bookwyrm paused before saying 'I had nothing to do with it.' This was not an alibi — it was a denial of complicity. The pause suggests she knows more than she admits. She may have been present, or she may have authorized access to the Keeper. Her role is ambiguous — protector, conspirator, or victim of a larger scheme.

subject: Bookwyrm's Pause
fact: When Thorin asked 'Where were you?', Bookwyrm paused — just long enough to weigh something. That pause is the most significant moment in the interrogation so far, and the narrator chose not to write down what it meant — but took notes anyway.
source_quote: I did not write down what I thought her expression meant... But I took notes.

subject: brain-based communication
fact: There is a theoretical possibility of communicating with the corpse using only the brain, bypassing the missing heart, but prior attempts have failed.
source_quote: We don't need the heart — we just need the brain to be able to talk to him, you know.

subject: Brother Heslin or Brother Arrath
fact: It is unclear whether Brother Heslin or Brother Arrath ran the theory sessions on repurposed threat.
source_quote: I wasn't sure the monks at the Garden Shadow would have approved of the metaphor, but Brother Heslin — or possibly Brother Arrath, I was never certain which of them ran the theory sessions on repurposed threat — had said something along those lines once.

subject: Daz's suspicion of Bookwyrm
fact: Daz notes that Bookwyrm volunteered information about Kalan's resignation at a strategic moment.
source_quote: She delivered it like a gift. Information, freely offered, before anyone had thought to ask.

subject: door left ajar on third floor
fact: The door to the third floor apartment was left conspicuously ajar, suggesting deliberate access or a distraction.
source_quote: a large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar. I noted the apartment. Noted that the door was open. Filed it for later.

subject: fixed points
fact: Grygum references 'fixed points' as a possible theological framework for the investigation.
source_quote: It could be one of those fixed points

subject: Fourth school of thought
fact: A fourth school of thought has been proposed — that the universe contains fixed points of cosmic constraint, around which mortal actions must revolve, with freedom existing only between them, and the architecture of belief subtly shaping evidence to enforce invariance.
source_quote: What if there are certain fixed points around which our actions must revolve? And the closer we come to one of those fixed points, the more constrained we are, but between them, perhaps we have a great deal of freedom of action.

subject: Gate Warden removed before questioning
fact: The Gate Warden was removed from his position before being questioned about what he found during his inspection.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: Glabbagool's ontological status
fact: The nature of an ooze’s consciousness, its capacity for discipline, and the meaning of its desire for freedom remain unexplored, creating a metaphysical mystery.
source_quote: I didn't know what *out* meant for an ooze. Neither did he. But the want was there.

subject: Grygumite School
fact: The Grygumite School is a newly declared school of thought that captured the council's interest.
source_quote: I am the head of the Grygumite School." A beat. "Founder, in fact.

subject: Grygum school of thought
fact: The Grygum school of thought is filed under things that started as offhand remarks.
source_quote: The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: heart removal to prevent resurrection
fact: The removal of Janussi's heart was deliberate to prevent resurrection rituals from working.
source_quote: Grygum named the precaution out loud, and once he said it I couldn't believe I hadn't thought of it first: you can't bring someone back from death by ritual if their vital organs aren't present.

subject: identity of the killer
fact: The killer was likely someone familiar with the chamber’s protocols, able to enter without raising suspicion, and knew to preserve the scene. The absence of forced entry, the timing of the smoke and candles, and the deliberate removal of the notes suggest an insider — possibly someone who had access to the study and knew Janussi’s work.
source_quote: Nobody smokes in a sealed room and leaves smoke that lingers for hours unless the room has been sealed for hours.

subject: identity of the murderer
fact: The identity of the murderer remains unknown, with no consensus among the Council, and the party’s arrival has introduced unverified external variables into the investigation.
source_quote: First, we must find the murderer!

subject: inventory of unfulfilled prophecies
fact: The fate of Candlekeep's prophecy archive when the inventory runs out remains unknown, posing a foundational theological and existential question.
source_quote: Nobody knew what happened when the inventory ran out.

subject: Kalan's Eyes Were Not
fact: Kalan Strongbranch’s bow was correct, but his eyes were not — a silent, potent indicator of hidden intent. This observation marks him as the primary subject of the narrator’s next move, and the thread of his loyalty or guilt remains unspoken.
source_quote: He was the first person I planned to question.

subject: legitimacy of Grygum’s authority
fact: Grygum’s claim to found the Grygumite School is unverified, and its sudden introduction into the Council’s crisis may be a deliberate distraction or an authentic intellectual incursion.
source_quote: I am the head of the Grygumite School." A beat. "Founder, in fact.

subject: Missing Heart
fact: Janussi’s heart was removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection — the motive suggests the killer intended to ensure permanent death, raising the question of who had the knowledge and means to perform such an act — and why.
source_quote: They wanted Janussi to stay dead in every sense that mattered.

subject: motive for murder
fact: The murder appears to have been motivated by the theft of Janussi’s most recent research — specifically the notes on The Golden Ass, written in midnight blue ink. The victim’s chest was hollowed out, suggesting the object removed was not jewelry but something tied to his research — possibly a magical artifact or component.
source_quote: Whatever he took, it wasn't jewelry... That felt deliberate in the way that things feel deliberate when you stop trying to find an innocent explanation for them.

subject: nature of the stolen object
fact: The object removed from Janussi’s chest was not jewelry — it was likely a magical artifact or component tied to his research on The Golden Ass. The hollow in his chest and the missing notes together suggest the killer sought a physical manifestation of the magic he was studying — perhaps a soul-bound glyph, a spell core, or a living inscription.
source_quote: There was a hollow in his chest where something used to be... Whatever he took, it wasn't jewelry.

subject: new philosophy of the universe
fact: Grygum claims to have found a new philosophy of the universe.
source_quote: And I have found a new philosophy of the universe.

subject: Poirot and Colombo
fact: Thorin and Grygum claim to be students of the great Masters Poirot and Colombo.
source_quote: Thorin said we were students of the great Masters Poirot and Colombo

subject: prophecy inventory
fact: Candlekeep recites unfulfilled prophecies from Alaundo's inventory.
source_quote: What remained was the unfulfilled inventory.

subject: protocol failure
fact: Tadric’s admission that his role was crowd control, not surveillance, reveals a critical failure in crime scene protocol. No one was monitoring what individuals did once inside — allowing the killer to remove the notes and the object without detection.
source_quote: Tadric admitted his job had been crowd control, not surveillance — watching who came in and out, not watching what they did once they were inside.

subject: repurposed threat
fact: Brother Heslin or Brother Arrath taught a theory about repurposing dangerous entities into knowledge repositories.
source_quote: Brother Heslin — or possibly Brother Arrath, I was never certain which of them ran the theory sessions on repurposed threat — had said something along those lines once.

subject: resurrection prevention
fact: The heart was removed not as a trophy but as a deliberate act to ensure Janussi could not be resurrected, implying the killer intended permanent death.
source_quote: They wanted Janussi to stay dead in every sense that mattered.

subject: strong-weak hypothesis
fact: Vareth names the proposed theological theory the 'strong-weak hypothesis'.
source_quote: He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: The Ajar Door
fact: The third-floor apartment door was left open — unexamined and unexplained — potentially connected to the murder, the missing book, or the cat’s behavior; it remains the next critical location to investigate.
source_quote: That was where I needed to be.

subject: The cat on the stairs
fact: The cat had been observed tracking the party without moving, and its nature as a potential power or familiar remained unproven and unresolved.
source_quote: Nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not.

subject: The Cat's Nature
fact: The cat’s behavior and the conflicting interpretations of it by the party suggest a hidden supernatural truth; its persistence, indifference, and the theological debate surrounding it imply it is more than it appears — or that someone wants others to believe it is.
source_quote: That's kind of how cats always are, I think," I said, because it is.

subject: the dragon scale building’s origin
fact: The Drakonoikos is built from dragon scales and bones — not mere decoration, but structural material. Who killed the dragon? Why were its remains used? Is this connected to Dawnbringer? To the Astronomicon’s celestial records? To the death of the Avowed? The building is a physical artifact of a hidden history that may hold the key to the murder.

subject: The Garden Shadow's curriculum
fact: The Garden Shadow never specified in their curriculum the conditions under which the party trained.
source_quote: After months of training under conditions the Garden Shadow had never specified in their curriculum, a few flights was nothing.

subject: The Gate Warden's Discovery
fact: The Gate Warden exited the crime scene after his inspection with a demeanor of discovery, yet was removed before reporting; his findings remain unknown, making him the most critical unspoken witness.
source_quote: Tadric noted that Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: The Gate Warden’s Secret
fact: The Gate Warden performed the 'Speak with Dead' ritual and left the scene determined — he knows something no one else does, and his removal from the investigation before debriefing suggests suppression or fear.
source_quote: He looked more determined after he walked out.

subject: The Grygum School of Thought
fact: A new theological framework — the Grygum school — has emerged as an accidental proposition, positing fixed cosmic points that constrain agency while allowing freedom between them; it is now being treated as the central question of Candlekeep’s age, with Vareth actively researching it.
source_quote: The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: The Grygum school of thought
fact: The Grygum school of thought was proposed as an offhand remark and is now being treated as the question of the age.
source_quote: I just proposed a school of theological thought by accident, and an aging scholar with forty-one years in this corner of the library is now treating it as the question of the age.

subject: The identity and purpose of the Drakonoikos
fact: The Drakonoikos is mentioned but not explained — its nature, function, or significance in Candlekeep remains an unresolved mystery.
source_quote: Then the Drakonoikos.

subject: The Identity of the Heart Seller
fact: The prophecy 'the heart is sold' remains unexplained, creating a second layer of mystery beyond the Keeper’s death — suggesting that a betrayal or sacrifice of institutional integrity is imminent or already underway.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.*

subject: The Missing Book
fact: 'The Golden Ass' is gone — the book Janussi was annotating with fresh ink — and its absence implies the research contained within was dangerous, heretical, or valuable enough to be stolen.
source_quote: Whatever Janussi had been working on most recently... was gone. That felt deliberate.

subject: the missing resignation record
fact: Bookwyrm revealed that Janussi requested Kalan’s resignation the morning of his death, but no written record of it was produced. The timing suggests it may have been destroyed or never documented — a deliberate act. The absence of this record is a critical gap in the investigation and may point to internal corruption or a cover-up.

subject: the nature of negligence
fact: Janussi accused Kalan of negligence, but the type of negligence was never specified. Was it failure to monitor the Dragon Breath Chamber? Allow unauthorized access? Neglect the Avowed? Or something more esoteric — like ignoring celestial signs recorded in the Astronomicon? The ambiguity is intentional and conceals a deeper institutional failure.

subject: The Nature of the Emerald Door
fact: The emerald door is a restricted passage used for clandestine access, implying that the First Reader operates outside standard institutional channels; its existence and use raise questions about hidden power structures within Candlekeep’s scholarly hierarchy.
source_quote: through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Need to Enter
fact: The party has not yet entered the third-floor apartment; its open door, proximity to the crime scene, and lack of documentation make it the next logical point of inquiry — the place where answers may be hidden.
source_quote: I hadn't been inside yet. That was where I needed to be.

subject: The Ooze’s Awakening
fact: Glabbagool’s desire to be released from the bag of holding signals a nascent sentience and existential yearning — potentially mirroring the Grygum school’s idea of constrained freedom — and may foreshadow his role in a larger theological or metaphysical revelation.
source_quote: He wanted out. I didn't know what *out* meant for an ooze. Neither did he. But the want was there.

subject: The Open Door
fact: The open door of the third-floor apartment is an unexplained anomaly in a highly controlled environment; its purpose and contents are unknown, but its existence implies a deliberate act or hidden evidence.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: The open door on the third floor
fact: The door to the apartment on the third floor landing had been left conspicuously ajar, and its significance had not yet been explained.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: the party’s philosophical framing
fact: Grygum and Thorin framed their investigation through pop culture (Poirot, Colombo) and philosophical claims — suggesting they are not just solving a crime, but testing a worldview. The murder may be a symptom of a deeper philosophical rupture in Candlekeep’s doctrine — perhaps between knowledge-as-control and knowledge-as-reverence. The party’s methods may be the solution, not just the means.

subject: the strong-weak hypothesis
fact: The theological framework of 'strong-weak' positions toward fixed points, derived from Stroud and Bahamut, was accidentally proposed as a school of thought and now stands as an unresolved doctrinal structure.
source_quote: I feel like I handled that competently," I say, to no one in particular. The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: The Unfulfilled Prophecy Inventory
fact: Candlekeep maintains an inventory of unfulfilled prophecies from Alaundo; the recitation of 'the keeper falls' immediately after the Keeper’s death suggests that prophecies are not mere predictions but active, self-fulfilling mechanisms within the universe’s architecture.
source_quote: What remained was the unfulfilled inventory. Nobody knew what happened when the inventory ran out.

subject: The Unobserved Gap
fact: Tadric admitted he was not observing, only controlling; the Gate Warden’s movements inside the chamber during his inspection were unrecorded; this gap in observation is the most significant vulnerability in the timeline.
source_quote: He had not been watching closely enough to track what he'd done in there.

subject: The Unspoken Protection
fact: The Council had been protecting something — access, knowledge, or perhaps a person — without realizing it. The request for full library access exposed this, and the murder became secondary to the revelation of institutional concealment.
source_quote: We had not realized we were protecting.

subject: tobacco smoke lingering
fact: Lingering tobacco smoke in the sealed Keeper's Chambers indicated the murder occurred hours before discovery.
source_quote: The windows were shut. Nobody had been smoking recently. The smoke was old. ... Nobody smokes in a sealed room and leaves smoke that lingers for hours unless the room has been sealed for hours.

subject: Why the First Reader chose Daz and Grygum
fact: The First Reader bypassed institutional channels to summon Daz and Grygum specifically — the reason for this trust remains unexplained and must be answered.
source_quote: The question of why she thought that was, I noted, a question I would need answered.
